segs.p: Dīgha Nikāya 7
segs.e: Long Discourses 7

segs.p: Jāliyasutta
segs.e: With Jāliya

segs.p: Evaṁ me sutaṁ—
segs.e: So I have heard.

segs.p: ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā kosambiyaṁ viharati ghositārāme.
segs.e: At one time the Buddha was staying near Kosambī in Ghosita’s monastery.

segs.p: Tena kho pana samayena dve pabbajitā—
segs.e: Now at that time two renunciates—

segs.p: muṇḍiyo ca paribbājako jāliyo ca dārupattikantevāsī yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkamiṁsu; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavatā saddhiṁ sammodiṁsu.
segs.e: the wanderer Muṇḍiya and Jāliya, the pupil of the wood-bowl ascetic—came to the Buddha and exchanged greetings with him.

segs.p: Sammodanīyaṁ kathaṁ sāraṇīyaṁ vītisāretvā ekamantaṁ aṭṭhaṁsu. Ekamantaṁ ṭhitā kho te dve pabbajitā bhagavantaṁ etadavocuṁ:
segs.e: When the greetings and polite conversation were over, they stood to one side and said to the Buddha,

segs.p: “kiṁ nu kho, āvuso gotama, taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīraṁ, udāhu aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran”ti?
segs.e: “Reverend Gotama, are the soul and the body one and the same, or is the soul one thing, the body another?”

segs.p: “Tena hāvuso, suṇātha sādhukaṁ manasi karotha, bhāsissāmī”ti.
segs.e: “Well then, reverends, listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

segs.p: “Evamāvuso”ti kho te dve pabbajitā bhagavato paccassosuṁ.
segs.e: “Yes, reverend,” they replied.

segs.p: Bhagavā etadavoca:
segs.e: The Buddha said this:

segs.p: “idhāvuso, tathāgato loke uppajjati arahaṁ, sammāsambuddho …pe…
segs.e: “Take the case when a Realized One arises in the world, perfected, a fully awakened Buddha …

segs.p: Evaṁ kho, āvuso, bhikkhu sīlasampanno hoti.
segs.e: That’s how a mendicant is accomplished in ethics. …

segs.p: …pe…
Paṭhamaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: They enter and remain in the first absorption …

segs.p: Yo kho, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, kallaṁ nu kho tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’?”

segs.p: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, kallaṁ tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: “It would, reverend.”

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
Ahaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, evaṁ jānāmi evaṁ passāmi.
segs.e: “But reverends, I know and see like this.

segs.p: Atha ca panāhaṁ na vadāmi:
segs.e: Nevertheless, I do not say:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vā …pe…
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’. …

segs.p: dutiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: They enter and remain in the second absorption …

segs.p: tatiyaṁ jhānaṁ …
segs.e: third absorption …

segs.p: catutthaṁ jhānaṁ upasampajja viharati.
segs.e: fourth absorption.

segs.p: Yo kho, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, kallaṁ nu kho tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti?
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’?”

segs.p: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati kallaṁ, tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: “It would, reverend.”

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
Ahaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, evaṁ jānāmi evaṁ passāmi.
segs.e: “But reverends, I know and see like this.

segs.p: Atha ca panāhaṁ na vadāmi:
segs.e: Nevertheless, I do not say:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vā …pe…
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’. …

segs.p: ñāṇadassanāya cittaṁ abhinīharati abhininnāmeti …
segs.e: They project and extend the mind toward knowledge and vision …

segs.p: yo kho, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, kallaṁ nu kho tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’?”

segs.p: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati kallaṁ tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: “It would, reverend.”

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
Ahaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, evaṁ jānāmi evaṁ passāmi.
segs.e: “But reverends, I know and see like this.

segs.p: Atha ca panāhaṁ na vadāmi:
segs.e: Nevertheless, I do not say:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vā …pe….
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’. …

segs.p: …pe… Nāparaṁ itthattāyāti pajānāti.
segs.e: They understand: ‘… there is nothing further for this place.’

segs.p: Yo kho, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, kallaṁ nu kho tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: When a mendicant knows and sees like this, would it be appropriate to say of them:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti?
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’?”

segs.p: Yo so, āvuso, bhikkhu evaṁ jānāti evaṁ passati, na kallaṁ tassetaṁ vacanāya:
segs.e: “It would not, reverend.”

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vāti.
Ahaṁ kho panetaṁ, āvuso, evaṁ jānāmi evaṁ passāmi.
segs.e: “But reverends, I know and see like this.

segs.p: Atha ca panāhaṁ na vadāmi:
segs.e: Nevertheless, I do not say:

segs.p: ‘taṁ jīvaṁ taṁ sarīran’ti vā ‘aññaṁ jīvaṁ aññaṁ sarīran’ti vā”ti.
segs.e: ‘The soul and the body are one and the same’ or ‘The soul is one thing, the body another’.”

segs.p: Idamavoca bhagavā.
segs.e: That is what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Attamanā te dve pabbajitā bhagavato bhāsitaṁ abhinandunti.
segs.e: Satisfied, the two renunciates approved what the Buddha said.

segs.p: Jāliyasuttaṁ niṭṭhitaṁ sattamaṁ.
